h1: The 6 Best Widescreen Monitor Privacy Screens of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 privacy screens for 16:9 widescreen monitors in 21.5, 24 and 27 inch sizes, compared on pack size, fit and price tier.
summary: For a dual 24 inch desk, the Peslv 2-pack is our top pick, with a removable design that suits screens you sometimes share. The unbranded 24 inch 2-pack is a close alternative. Single-monitor users should buy the SightPro 24 or SightPro 27 to match their screen, and dual 27 inch setups get the most value from the blue light 2-pack.
intro: Privacy filters get returned for one reason more than any other, and it is not quality. People order by diagonal and forget the shape. A 24 inch filter cut for a 16:9 widescreen leaves a strip uncovered on a 24 inch 16:10 display and overhangs the bezel. Measure twice, and check the aspect ratio printed on your monitor's spec sheet before anything else.

Once the fit is right, the decision is mostly about how many screens you cover and what extras you want. We reviewed six filters built for 16:9 monitors, from dual 24 inch packs to a single 21.5 inch panel, and scored each on the Primea framework. Size coverage, pack value, mounting method and extras like blue light filtering drove the rankings.

products.name: Peslv 2-Pack 24 Inch Privacy Screen for Computer Monitor, 16:9 Aspect Ratio
products.description:
The Peslv kit covers two 24 inch 16:9 monitors in one order, and both filters are removable, so they come off when you need to share your screen with a colleague. It sits in the $50 to $100 tier.

It ranks first because it solves the most common office setup completely. Most people who need privacy work across two monitors, and buying singles separately costs about the same with more hassle. Against the unbranded 2-pack below, Peslv is clearer about the removable mounting, which is what you want when filters come on and off through the day.

Buy it for a dual 24 inch desk in an open office, a reception area or anywhere screens face a walkway. The caveat is fit: confirm both monitors are true 16:9 panels before you order.

products.name: 2 Pack 24 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 16:9 Widescreen Monitor
products.description:
This 2-pack covers the same ground as the Peslv: two filters sized for 24 inch 16:9 widescreen monitors, in the $50 to $100 tier. It is built for dual-screen desks.

It ranks second because the listing gives less detail on how the filters attach and whether they are designed to be removed often. For a desk where the filters go on once and stay put, that makes little difference. For shared screens, the Peslv's clearer removable design wins.

Buy it if the Peslv is out of stock or this pack is cheaper on the day, and you plan to leave the filters on permanently. Skip it if you will be taking filters on and off several times a week. Either way, measure your viewable area first.

products.name: SightPro 24 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter for Monitor
products.verdict: A single 24 inch filter in the lower tier.
products.description:
SightPro's 24 inch filter is the single-screen pick in the most common monitor size. It is cut for 16:9 panels and sells as one unit in the $25 to $50 tier.

It ranks third behind the two-packs because most people who need a filter run two monitors, and a single unit only covers half of that setup. For a one-monitor desk, though, it is the better buy: you pay for one filter, not two, from a brand that specializes in screen filters.

Buy it if you work on a single 24 inch widescreen, or a laptop plus one external monitor where only the monitor needs privacy. If you have two matching 24 inch displays, a 2-pack like the Peslv is better value than buying this twice.

products.name: SightPro 27 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter for Monitor
products.verdict: A single 27 inch filter for big monitors.
products.description:
This SightPro filter is the larger sibling of the 24 inch model, sized for 27 inch 16:9 monitors. It sells as a single unit in the $25 to $50 tier.

It ranks fourth simply because it serves a narrower group. A 27 inch monitor is common, but less so than 24 inch at work, and this filter covers only one screen. It is the cleanest single-unit option here for a larger display, and it carries the same SightPro focus on filters as the 24 inch model.

Buy it if you have one 27 inch widescreen and want a dedicated filter from a known filter brand. If you have two 27 inch displays, the blue light 2-pack below covers both for a similar tier. Check that your monitor is 16:9, since some 27 inch panels are not.

products.name: 2 Pack 27 Inch Computer Monitor Privacy Screen, Blue Light Filter
products.verdict: A 27 inch 2-pack with blue light filtering.
products.description:
This 2-pack is sized for 27 inch 16:9 monitors and adds blue light filtering on top of privacy. It sits in the $25 to $50 tier, the same as a single SightPro 27.

It ranks fifth because the brand is unknown, so build quality and coating durability are harder to judge than with SightPro. On pure value, though, it is hard to beat: two filters plus blue light reduction for the price of one name-brand panel.

Buy it for a dual 27 inch setup, or if you want a spare filter for a second desk. Remember that blue light filtering is a comfort extra and does nothing for privacy. Skip it if you want proven coating quality and are happy to pay for a single SightPro.

products.name: Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 21.5 Inch 16:9 Aspect Ratio Monitor
products.verdict: A single filter for 21.5 inch widescreens.
products.description:
The last pick is a single filter for 21.5 inch 16:9 monitors, a size common on older office displays and compact all-in-one computers. Price lands in the $25 to $50 tier.

The narrow fit is why it ranks last: it fits the fewest screens here. Nothing about it is wrong, but 21.5 inch is a shrinking size, and the listing offers few extras. If your monitor is that size, though, a 24 inch filter simply will not work, so this becomes the only sensible choice in the lineup.

Buy it for a 21.5 inch 16:9 monitor at a reception desk, a point of sale terminal or a home office with an older display. Measure the visible screen area first, since bezels and panel tolerances vary.

whatMatters.detail: Aspect ratio is the width-to-height shape of your display, such as 16:9 or 16:10. Filters are cut to one ratio, so a 16:9 filter on a 16:10 screen leaves a gap at the top or bottom. That gap defeats the privacy effect. Find your monitor's ratio in its spec sheet or the manufacturer's page, not on the box.

Filters are sized by screen diagonal, but what really counts is the visible area inside the bezel. Two monitors sold as 24 inch can differ slightly. Measure the visible width and height with a tape and compare them to the filter's listed dimensions. A filter that is a few millimeters too large will not sit flush and may slip.

A 2-pack covers a dual-monitor desk in one order and usually costs less than two singles. It can also give you a spare for a home office. Check whether the listing title says 2 pack or two filters, and confirm both are the same size, since some bundles mix sizes.

Some filters add a coating that reduces blue light from the screen. That can feel easier on the eyes over a long day, but it has nothing to do with blocking side views. Treat it as a bonus, not a reason to buy. Look for blue light in the title or feature bullets, as on the 27 inch 2-pack.

Filters attach with adhesive strips, slide-in tabs or hanging clips. Removable designs let you take the filter off to share the screen and put it back quickly. Adhesive mounts stay put but are harder to remove cleanly. Check the photos and bullets for the attachment method, and confirm the tabs suit your bezel depth.

faq.q: Do privacy screens fit all monitors?
faq.a: No. Each filter must match both your screen size and aspect ratio. A 16:9 filter like the SightPro 24 will not sit correctly on a 16:10 monitor. Check your monitor's spec sheet before ordering, and measure the visible area if in doubt.

Ignoring aspect ratio and ordering by diagonal alone. The second most common mistake is buying two singles for a dual setup when a 2-pack like the Peslv covers both screens for similar money and ships together.

For two matching monitors, yes. The Peslv and the 27 inch blue light pack cover both screens for roughly the price of one name-brand single. For a single monitor, a SightPro 24 or SightPro 27 is the better buy.

Clean the screen with a microfiber cloth, attach the tabs or strips to the bezel, then slide or hang the filter in place. Removable designs like the Peslv let you lift it off and refit it in seconds. Avoid pressing hard on the panel.

Wipe it with a dry or slightly damp microfiber cloth. Avoid alcohol-based or ammonia sprays, which can damage the coating. Store removable filters like the Peslv flat when not in use so they do not warp or scratch.

Yes, slightly. Privacy filters narrow the viewing angle, so the screen looks a little darker head-on and much darker from the side. Most people turn monitor brightness up a notch to compensate. The effect is similar across the SightPro and Peslv filters.

finalTake: For most dual 24 inch desks, the Peslv 2-pack is the filter set to buy: removable, well sized and fair value for two screens. Single-monitor users should match the SightPro 24 or 27 to their display. Dual 27 inch setups get the most for the money from the blue light 2-pack, and older 21.5 inch screens have their own dedicated option. Measure first, then order.
